record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Does there exist a real-analytic diffeomorphism of either the cylinder T^1 × [−1,1] or the sphere S^2 that is homotopic to the identity, preserves Lebesgue measure, has only finitely many periodic orbits, and nevertheless has a dense orbit?

evidence.quote: 3.1 - Question. Does there exist a Cω(= R-analytic)-diﬀeomorphism, homotopic to the identity, Lebesgue measure-preserving, of T1×[−1, 1] orS2, with a ﬁnite number of periodic orbits and a dense orbit ?

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned recent work on generic density of periodic points and on periodic orbits of area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms (using ECH/PFH tools by Cristofaro-Gardiner, Prasad, Zhang and others), but no source was found that constructs or rules out a real-analytic, Lebesgue-preserving, identity-homotopic diffeomorphism of the cylinder or sphere having only finitely many periodic orbits together with a dense orbit. The status appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Generic Density of Periodic Orbits of Area-preserving Maps on Punctured Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative equidistribution and generic density results for area-preserving maps on surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related work concerns periodic-orbit density for area-preserving surface maps, but does not address the real-analytic finite-periodic-orbits-with-dense-orbit question.

status_evidence.title: Action and rotation number of periodic orbits of area-preserving annulus diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodic orbits of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the annulus.
status_evidence.claim: Recent annulus results focus on existence/properties of periodic orbits but do not resolve the analytic dense-orbit question.
